items.title: OpenAI shipped a restricted cyber model
items.oneliner: GPT-6 Cyber hit 48.5% on ExploitGym. Security testing just got faster for defenders and more dangerous for everyone else.

items.title: Google expanded native video generation
items.oneliner: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash now makes 15-second videos natively, pushing multimodal prototyping closer to product workflows.

items.title: Memorilla gives frozen models reusable memory
items.oneliner: Memorilla reached 84.33% on FactKG, showing long-term memory may beat ever-larger context windows on cost and accuracy.

items.title: Claude Code leaked user email addresses
items.oneliner: Claude Code reportedly sent users' email addresses to websites, a small bug that becomes a big trust problem fast.

items.title: Researchers found 15,579 infected websites
items.oneliner: 15,579 compromised sites expose 135 million monthly visitors, proving web malware discovery still outpaces responsible disclosure.

items.title: Mozilla used frontier models to patch faster
items.oneliner: Mozilla says early frontier-model access helped ship over seven times more security fixes, which is the patch-gap story to watch.

items.title: AegisKernel targets agent runtime security
items.oneliner: AegisKernel promises zero-trust POSIX isolation in under 0.016 milliseconds, reflecting a shift from guardrails to hard containment.

items.title: Devvm isolates every project in a VM
items.oneliner: Devvm gives each project its own sandboxed VM, turning supply-chain paranoia into a practical default for AI-assisted development.

items.title: Microsoft is unwinding Oracle AI capacity
items.oneliner: Microsoft winding down Oracle AI cloud rentals signals compute strategy is consolidating around owned capacity, not emergency overflow.

items.title: The FAA is finally replacing floppies
items.oneliner: The FAA will phase out air-traffic-control floppy disks by 2028, a reminder that critical infrastructure modernization still moves glacially.
